belongs_to: "But how much is one lakh? Observe the pattern and fill in the boxes given below." (largest / smallest n-digit numbers, +1 arrows)
description: Six rows stacked vertically. Each row has a label box on the left (white box with blue outline, light-blue dashed ribbon edge along its top and bottom, and a blue right-pointing arrow tab on its right edge) and a value box on the right (white rectangle with blue outline). Row 1: label 'The largest 3-digit number is', value box shows 999 (filled). Row 2: label 'The smallest 4-digit number is', value box EMPTY. Row 3: label 'The largest 4-digit number is', value box EMPTY. Row 4: label 'The smallest 5-digit number is', value box EMPTY. Row 5: label 'The largest 5-digit number is', value box EMPTY. Row 6: label 'The smallest 6-digit number is', value box shows 1,00,000 (filled). Three curved blue arrows on the right side of the value boxes, each labelled '+1': one from the value box of row 1 (999) down to the value box of row 2; one from the value box of row 3 down to the value box of row 4; one from the value box of row 5 down to the value box of row 6 (1,00,000). So 3 arrows in total, and no arrow between rows 2-3 or 4-5. Centred bold-italic caption under the six rows: '1,00,000 is read as "One Lakh"'. Total value boxes: 6 (2 filled: 999 and 1,00,000; 4 empty).

belongs_to: "Getting a Feel of Large Numbers": "Look at the picture on the right. Somu is 1 metre tall. If each floor is about four times his height, what is the approximate height of the building?"
description: A tall, narrow red-brick building drawn full height along the right margin of the page. A flat tan roof slab on top. 10 stacked floors, each with one dark arched window with a cream frame, a white railing balcony in front of it and a tan balcony slab below it. At the foot, below the 10th balcony, a tan double door (ground level). On the balcony of the TOP floor a very small boy (Somu) stands waving one arm; a white speech bubble to its left points at him and reads 'Hi! I am Somu.' No height marks, ticks or numbers are printed on the building itself.
unclear: Whether the ground-level double-door strip counts as an extra floor beyond the 10 balcony floors is not stated; 10 balcony/window floors were counted on the picture.
The building is a cartoon; the book gives no scale on it other than 'Somu is 1 metre tall' and 'each floor is about four times his height'.

belongs_to: "Which is taller - The Statue of Unity or this building? How much taller?"; "How much taller is the Kunchikal waterfall than Somu's building?"; "How many floors should Somu's building have to be as high as the waterfall?"
description: An illustration (about 375 × 360 px on the page) with a vertical measuring scale on its left edge. Scale: a black vertical axis line; tick labels, evenly spaced, from bottom to top: 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 (numbers sit to the left of the axis; there are no tick marks other than the three horizontal lines below); rotated axis title 'meters' written upright-sideways along the axis between the 200 and 300 labels. Three black horizontal reference lines start at the axis: (a) at the 500 level: a long line across to the top of the middle waterfall stream; (b) at the 200 level: a medium line ending at the head of the grey Statue of Unity; (c) a short line at a level between 0 and 100 (about 60 by eye) ending at the top of a thin pink vertical strip with tiny dashes standing on the ground between the cliff and the statue (apparently a miniature of Somu's building). Scene: a rock cliff with green hill on top and blue hills behind; three white-cyan waterfall streams (left one with a small fork, a middle one, a right one) falling into a pool at the base; the statue (grey standing figure on a low pale pedestal, ground level = 0) stands at the left foot of the cliff, left of the pool. No other numbers or labels.
unclear: Line (c) height is read by eye (about 60 m, between the 0 and 100 labels) and not stated in the text.
The pink strip beside the statue is assumed to be a scaled miniature of Somu's building; its dashes (about 8-10) are too small to count reliably.
The text says the statue is about 180 m and the waterfall about 450 m, but the picture's reference lines sit at the 200 and 500 labels; which reading the book intends is not clear.
